asr.full_text: Namaste, I am Latika and today I am going to show you how to make besan poli. I have taken 1 cup of besan flour and 1 small cup of rice flour. Add besan flour of your choice as well. We have made this at home but it does not make a different. It contains 2 Tbsp rice flour. Use this for your breakfast as well. You can also add it to chapati or rice, if you feel like it. Finely chop 1 onion. You can serve with a chyapaathi or bakari or serve it with rice for an easy bite Make sure you cut these onions really finely Even though, the amount of garlic is not sufficient, its okay to let it be You can squeeze it instead of using garlic Salt to taste Pinch of Asafoetida We have used 2 pinches of Dried Clove Green chillies, Garlic, a pinch of Cumin Seeds A pinch of Coriander Add all of this So what we, some cumin, coriander leaves and a pinch of turmeric powder Make sure it is not too thick Once the pan has heated up, turn the flame low Pour a small quantity of the mixture Do not apply oil on the pan Take a thin layer of the batter The pan is hot now Like this It's good to make it as thin as possible As we've added onion in it And if you didn't use any special flour then it's okay If you want to know more about this try tell me by commenting in the comment box And if you saw this recipe do Like and Comment And don't forget to do So Now on mid flame increase the flame into low so we have to use low flame turn the flame medium after that oil is applied on it so gently drop the oil stir it and fry it if you do chapati or goat how do you are cooking in a pan Don't add too much of oil Rub the pan to rub it properly This tawa turns out like this And when you do something like this it turns out nicely Let's flip it Look at this, how nicely golden brown it has become Turn the flame to medium keep stirring can see it is cooked nicely gas is medium earlier i used to use very small flame now use the medium flame after coating of Poli after cooking on medium flame we don't add extra oil you can also burn the vegetable oil we will also keep stirring Also you can do the same for oil Make a nice one If it doesn't roast well, you can press once Also it requires a precise taste It is convenient for making Varan Bhata or Tondi Also it is suitable for breakfast We can see the batter is crispy Press it to see if it is roasted well Turn over and see See it is roasted well It should be fine Roast it a little It should not be as hard as normal It will still prepare nicely If you do not like rice flour Make light-weight chapatis if needed, then make them more thick. We are not trying to make the chapati as thick, just enough to enjoy it. You can also omit some, if you don't have it. I am cooking this as a veg break, so I have used a little rice flour in it. Everything looks thick and nice. These are nicely roasted. I have also made the Ghatta Vali. I have made the Ghatta Vali as thin as a layer of water. I will show you how to make it. And we have roasted all of the parts You can now take the dal and make them into thin slabs This is an easy way to keep the dal in the dish Because as I told earlier, we should show you how to make it The dal has become thin with no extra oil And we will use the rest of the fat Now we will grind all the ingredients See how thin it is We roast all of it Now we need to flip it You can see the thin layers. These make nice fat curdled curds. I'll roast it. Do it upside down as it is. Or place it over a lid for 1-2 minutes. See, how nice it's done. I won't apply oil on it, this way we'll roast it. Let's cook it. We didn't apply oil on it. Roast well, well-done. after a while check if its roasted enough it turned out very nicely this is without any oil must make the paste on pressing it here i could not press it i should press it now if the mixture is kept a bit raw it will be very nicely roasted here the oil is not used to make the paste nicely prepared i show all the process like this and if you like this recipe, do like, subscribe, comment and share
